engine.summary: 2D nesting of polygons on sheets and 3D packing of boxes in a container, by constructive fills and metaheuristic searches, with checkers that say whether a layout keeps its problem's rules.

surfaces.name: u-nesting
surfaces.error_shape: Err(Error), whose code() is the code and whose variant holds the fields.

surfaces.name: @iyulab/u-nesting
surfaces.note: Objects in and out, typed in the .d.ts (Request2D, SolveResponse, ...); a refusal is thrown. Bundler and Node targets; no bundler-less browser build.
surfaces.error_shape: A thrown Error whose code property is the code, with the fields as its other properties.

surfaces.name: u-nesting
surfaces.error_shape: Nothing raised: the response dict has success False, the code and a details dict holding the fields.

surfaces.name: UNesting
surfaces.note: C ABI wrapper; versioned with the crate.
surfaces.error_shape: A NestingException whose ErrorCode is the code, Parameter and Index the fields of those names, and Details the rest.

errors.shape: A refusal carries a stable snake_case 'code' and the fields listed for that code; how it arrives depends on the surface (error_shape).

source.catalog: CodeCatalog::of_engine in crates/core/src/api_types.rs, read off one example of every refusal and checker violation; published as codes() in WebAssembly and Python, unesting_codes() over the C ABI and Codes on .NET. What each code means is tabled in npm/README.md, which a test holds equal to the catalog.

operations.summary: Places polygon parts on a rectangular or polygonal sheet (or on as many sheets as they need), by the chosen strategy, and reports the placements, the parts left unplaced, the utilization and why the run stopped.

effects.note: The searches (ga, brkga, sa, gdrr, alns) draw from config.seed when it is given and from fresh entropy when it is not; blf and nfp use no randomness.

determinism.note: The worst case, for a search without config.seed. stop_reason says which limit ended a run.

cases.when: strategy blf or nfp, with time_limit_ms 0 (no time limit)
a search (ga, brkga, sa) given config.seed, with time_limit_ms 0: it ends on its own generation budget
strategy blf or nfp, with a time limit (time_limit_ms above 0)
cases.note: A fill stops before its next piece once the limit runs out, so how many pieces it places depends on machine speed; one that finishes in time gives the layout it gives without a limit.

cases.when: a search given config.seed, with a time limit (time_limit_ms above 0)
cases.note: How far the search gets before the limit depends on machine speed; with the same seed it visits the same candidates in the same order.

output_provenance.note: Whether the layout is a finished construction, the best a search found before a budget or the deadline, or a cancelled run's.

checks.claim: Every 2D strategy returns each piece inside the sheet and its margin, no two pieces overlapping or closer than the spacing, no copy placed twice, and the unplaced list, counts and utilization the placements add up to; the same holds on every sheet of a multi-sheet layout, where utilization is the placed area over each sheet's height times the length the pieces reach.
checks.reference: the definition of a feasible rectangular layout, by interval arithmetic that shares no code with the engine
checks.method: 7 strategies x two seeded six-piece sets (margin 0 and 1.5, spacing 0 and 0.5), and 7 multi-sheet runs on 14 x 14 sheets

checks.claim: Twenty-four 1 x 2 bars never pass full utilization or the count that fits in a 6 x 8 sheet.
checks.reference: area conservation: placed area cannot exceed the sheet
checks.method: every strategy on a perfectly tileable set

limits: Axis-aligned rectangles are checked exactly; layouts of non-rectangular polygons are checked by the engine's own checker (check_2d) only.
Layout quality has not been compared against best-known solutions of standard instances.

performance.complexity: Constructive fills: about O(n^2) no-fit-polygon queries in the part count n; searches: that per evaluated layout, until their budget or the deadline.

operations.summary: Packs boxes into a container by the chosen strategy (a layer fill, extreme points, or a GA, BRKGA or SA search), with orientations, spacing, margins, a mass limit and support under gravity, and reports the placements, the boxes left unplaced, the utilization and why the run stopped.

effects.note: The searches (ga, brkga, sa) draw from config.seed when it is given and from fresh entropy when it is not; blf and ep use no randomness.

determinism.note: The worst case, for a search without config.seed. stop_reason says which limit ended a run.

cases.when: strategy blf or ep, with time_limit_ms 0 (no time limit)
a search (ga, brkga, sa) given config.seed, with time_limit_ms 0: it ends on its own generation budget
strategy blf or ep, with a time limit (time_limit_ms above 0)
cases.note: A fill stops before its next box once the limit runs out, so how many boxes it places depends on machine speed; one that finishes in time gives the packing it gives without a limit.

cases.when: a search given config.seed, with a time limit (time_limit_ms above 0)
cases.note: How far the search gets before the limit depends on machine speed; with the same seed it visits the same candidates in the same order.

output_provenance.note: Whether the layout is a finished construction, the best a search found before a budget or the deadline, or a cancelled run's.

checks.claim: Every 3D strategy returns each box inside the container and its margin with no two boxes overlapping, the orientation label read as which original axis lies along each world axis, and utilization equal to the boxes' volume over the bins' volume.
checks.reference: the definition of a feasible box packing, by interval arithmetic that shares no code with the engine
checks.method: 5 strategies x two seeded five-box sets (margin 0 and 0.5)

limits: Mass, support (gravity, stability) and orientation constraints are covered by unit tests, not by this oracle.
Packing quality has not been compared against best-known solutions of standard instances.

performance.complexity: Constructive fills: polynomial in the box count (candidate positions times boxes); searches: that per evaluated packing, until their budget or the deadline.

operations.summary: Whether a 2D layout keeps the problem it answers -- the solve_2d request and its response: every part inside the sheet and its margin, no overlap (by intersection area) or spacing breach, allowed rotations and flips, the sheets and copies used, and the parts reported unplaced; lists every rule broken. Its problem schema is generated from the request type both dimensions share, so it lists 3D-only settings too; solve_2d's own request schema is exact.

checks.claim: On 60 layouts of rectangles dropped anywhere on the sheet, some feasible and some not, the pieces reported outside the sheet and the pairs reported overlapping are exactly those that interval arithmetic finds, and feasible is true exactly when there are none.
checks.reference: the definition of a feasible rectangular layout (containment and zero-area overlap)
checks.method: 60 seeded layouts: a third the solver's own, a third with one piece moved, a third with every piece moved

limits: Only boundary and overlap violations are compared with an independent predicate; the other violation kinds are covered by unit tests.

operations.summary: Whether a 3D packing keeps the problem it answers -- the solve_3d request and its response: every box inside the container and its margin, no overlap or spacing breach, allowed orientations, one container, copies, the mass limit, support under gravity and stability, and the boxes reported unplaced; lists every rule broken.

checks.claim: On 60 packings of boxes dropped anywhere in the container with random orientations, the boxes reported outside and the pairs reported overlapping are exactly those that interval arithmetic finds.
checks.reference: the definition of a feasible box packing (containment and zero-volume overlap)
checks.method: 60 seeded packings: a third the solver's own, a third with one box moved, a third with every box moved

limits: Only boundary and overlap violations are compared with an independent predicate; mass, support and orientation violations are covered by unit tests.

operations.summary: A cutting sequence for the parts a successful solve_2d placed: the order and direction of every contour (holes before the boundary around them, inner parts before outer ones), pierce points, rapid moves between them, and the contours it had to skip with the reason; the estimated time when speeds are given. A 2-opt pass improves the order until cutting_config.time_limit_ms (default 5000; 0 for none).

effects.note: The 2-opt improvement stops at cutting_config.time_limit_ms; computation_time_ms in the result measures the call.

determinism.note: The worst case, a time limit above 0 (the default is 5000 ms): how far the improvement gets depends on machine speed.

checks.claim: The plan cuts each placed part once, each step cuts the part's perimeter, each rapid starts where the previous cut ended and is as long as the move to the pierce point, and the totals (cut, rapid, pierces, time at the given speeds, efficiency) are what the steps add up to.
checks.reference: the definition of a cutting plan's figures
checks.method: six seeded four-piece layouts, kerf 0, rapid speed 50, cut speed 5

limits: The order of the cuts is not checked for optimality; kerf compensation, interior contours and home position are covered by unit tests.

output_provenance.note: Which contours the sequence leaves out and why.

operations.summary: The strategies each dimension offers in this build and the settings each reads; a solve giving any other setting with that strategy is refused.
